title: Establish multi-metric eval contracts and canary stop rules for Optimize
creator: Priya Desai
description: Purpose: Define concrete, operational eval contracts for the Optimize product so that model updates, quantization changes, and runtime parameter adjustments can be validated automatically before rollout. This ticket establishes the measurement surface (prompt sets, metrics, segmentation), acceptance gates for canary and broad rollout, statistical testing rules for A/B experiments, and automated rollback triggers. Goal is to reduce undetected regressions in customer-facing quality while preserving throughput/cost improvements.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical prompt set is defined for internal regression checks: 3 buckets (core-gen, long-context, adversarial) with at least 1,200 unique prompts total and explicit seeding rules to ensure reproducibility.

A multi-metric scoring function is agreed: weighted_score = 0.5 * quality + 0.2 * safety + 0.15 * factuality + 0.1 * latency_score + 0.05 * token_cost_score, where each component is normalized to 0-100.
Clear pass/fail bands established for canary: green (no metric regression beyond hard thresholds), yellow (soft regressions — requires manual review), red (fail — automatic rollback).
Automated canary pipeline executes for every Optimize-affecting change and produces a machine-readable report and human summary within 60 minutes of completion.
A/B test criteria (MDE, alpha, power, min-sample) documented and integrated into the console so product owners can run sequential tests without engineering changes.
Rollback rules wired into deployment orchestration: any red-level trigger during canary stops rollout and opens a P0 incident with attached eval artifacts.
Documentation and playbook (how to interpret Yellow results, run focused follow-ups, and rebaseline) are published and linked from Optimize release notes.
scope: Define prompt set composition, seeding, and refresh cadence (quarterly + event-driven).
Agree on metric definitions and normalization functions for quality, safety, factuality, latency, and token cost.
Specify canary pass/fail thresholds and the three-tier banding logic (green/yellow/red).
Design A/B testing guardrails (sequential testing approach, MDE, minimum exposure, segmenting by customer tier).
Create machine-readable evaluation report schema consumed by CI and Console dashboards.
Wire automatic rollback signals into the existing rollout orchestration and incident workflow.
out_of_scope: Model training or curator-level dataset changes (this ticket targets inference-time evals and rollout rules).
Large-scale UX changes to the Console beyond adding a small dashboard tile and links.
Billing model changes tied to Optimize pricing.
success_metrics: <2% of production model updates cause unplanned customer-facing regressions (measured by post-release quality alerts) over the next two quarters.
Canary evaluations complete end-to-end within 60 minutes for 95% of runs.
False-positive automatic rollbacks occur in <1% of rollouts (tracked and audited).
Adversarial prompt failure rate reduction: measured improvement of >=1.5 percentage points after adopting the new gating rules (within two releases).
rollout_plan: 1) Finalize prompt set and metric definitions with Research and Reliability teams (2 weeks).
2) Implement evaluation runner and machine-readable report in Optimize CI (3 weeks).
3) Add sequential A/B experiment config to Console with default MDE and alpha (2 weeks).
4) Pilot canary gating on one model family (one month), iterate thresholds based on pilot feedback.
5) Gradual enablement for all Optimize-affecting changes with mandatory canary for P0/P1-level changes, monitor first four production rollouts.
regression_thresholds: Weighted_score: absolute drop >1.0 points (on 0-100 scale) => YELLOW; >2.5 points => RED.
Safety regression (increase in unsafe outputs): >0.3 percentage points absolute => RED for any customer segment, >0.1pp => YELLOW.
Factuality drop (measured by benchmarked F1): relative drop >3% => RED.
Latency tail (p95) increase >30% or absolute >250ms => YELLOW; >50% or >400ms => RED.
Token cost efficiency regression (cost per 1k tokens): increase >8% => YELLOW; >15% => RED.
ab_test_criteria: Default statistical approach: group-sequential testing with alpha=0.025 (one-sided), power=0.9, and pre-specified MDE=1.5% for the weighted_score unless product owner overrides.
Minimum exposure for A/B: 50k impressions or 3 days, whichever is longer, unless overridden by product + risk review.
Tests must report both statistical significance and practical significance; no rollout on statistically significant but practically negligible differences.
Segmented checks required for enterprise customers: compute metrics per customer tier and abort/flag if any tier shows RED-level regression.
rollback_triggers: Automatic rollback (immediate stop) if any RED-level trigger fires during canary for production-critical segments.
Automatic pause and notify (require manual review) on YELLOW-level triggers for >=2 metrics in the same run.
Manual rollback recommended if post-A/B monitoring shows sustained customer complaints or support tickets correlated with the change in the first 48 hours.
Emergency rollback if safety regressions exceed 0.5pp in absolute terms for any public customer cohort.
